question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Key battlefields of the First and Second Carnatic Wars]
options: Battle of Adyar (1746) — fought near Madras between the French and the Nawab of Carnatic's forces
Battle of Ambur (1749) — fought near Vellore where Anwar-ud-din was defeated and killed
Battle of Kaveripak (1752) — fought near Arcot where Clive defeated French-allied forces
Battle of Buxar (1764) — fought near Patna as the decisive engagement of the First Carnatic War
wrong_fact: The Battle of Buxar (1764) was fought in Bihar (near Patna) and was part of the British expansion in Bengal/North India, not the First Carnatic War (which ended in 1748 and was fought in south India).
explanation: The Carnatic Wars were fought in southern India. The Battle of Adyar (1746) near Madras and Battle of Ambur (1749) near Vellore were key engagements. The Battle of Kaveripak (1752) near Arcot was a Clive victory. The Battle of Buxar (1764) took place in Bihar and involved the Bengal theater, completely unrelated to the Carnatic Wars.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Treaties ending the Carnatic Wars and their geographic terms]
options: Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle (1748) — Madras was returned to the British in exchange for Louisbourg in North America
Treaty of Pondicherry (1754) — French and British agreed not to interfere in the affairs of local princes
Treaty of Paris (1763) — French factories in India were restored but Pondicherry was permanently ceded to the British
Treaty of Westminster (1756) — neutralized the Carnatic region under joint Dutch-Danish administration
wrong_fact: There was no Treaty of Westminster in 1756 that neutralized the Carnatic under Dutch-Danish administration. The Carnatic Wars were primarily fought between the British and French, with no Dutch or Danish administration involved.
explanation: The Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle (1748) ended the First Carnatic War, restoring Madras to the British. The Treaty of Pondicherry (1754) ended the Second Carnatic War. The Treaty of Paris (1763) ended the Third Carnatic War, restoring French factories (including Pondicherry) but with military restrictions. The Treaty of Westminster (1756) was an Anglo-Prussian alliance in Europe and had nothing to do with Dutch-Danish control of the Carnatic.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Geographic logistics and military maneuvers during the Carnatic Wars]
options: Siege of Trichinopoly (1751–1752) — French-backed forces blockaded Muhammad Ali on the island of Srirangam
Clive's diversionary march to Arcot — Clive marched inland from Fort St. George, bypassing Pondicherry to draw forces away from Trichinopoly
Battle of Golden Rock — fought on the rocky heights near Madras to relieve the French siege of Fort St. George
Battle of Valdour — fought near Pondicherry where British forces countered French defensive lines
wrong_fact: The Battle of Golden Rock (1753) was fought near Trichinopoly (Tiruchirappalli) in southern Tamil Nadu, NOT near Madras. It was a key battle where Lawrence defeated the French under Astruc during the long siege of Trichinopoly.
explanation: Trichinopoly and Srirangam were the central focuses of the Second Carnatic War. Clive's march to Arcot diverted Chanda Sahib's forces. The Battle of Valdour was fought near Pondicherry. The Battle of Golden Rock (1753) was fought at Trichinopoly (specifically on the Golden Rock, a prominent hill near the city), not near Madras.
